headline: Wall Street took back the post Fed selloff, with the Nasdaq Composite up 1.69 percent and the 10 year Treasury yield down to 4.947 percent as Brent settled 1.7 percent lower at 104.03 dollars on Saudi pipeline repairs, and the Bank of Japan decides today with swaps pricing a quarter point hike to 1.25 percent.

summary.us: The S&P 500 rose 1.14 percent to 7,637.76 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.69 percent to 26,418.30, reversing Wednesday's drop after the Fed lifted the funds rate 25 basis points to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike since 2023, with Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish tone read as restoring inflation credibility. Falling oil did the heavy lifting: the 10 year yield slipped about 5 basis points to 4.947 percent after eight straight days of gains, the VIX fell 12.8 percent to 15.44, and single names moved on deals rather than macro, with Generac up 18 percent on an 8 billion dollar Amazon generator contract and Micron up 5 percent on memory supply commentary.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed 0.23 percent higher at 23,270.60 while the Sensex ended flat, down 21.86 points at 74,314.59, as gains in realty, pharma, auto and metals offset a banking drag and a 1 percent fall in TCS on the Fed's hawkish signal for IT spending. Life insurers led the tape on expectations that IRDAI lowers distributor commissions, taking HDFC Life up 5.05 percent and SBI Life up 4.06 percent while distributor PB Fintech fell 3.4 percent; the rupee was near 96.13 per dollar and foreign investors have sold 17,222 crore rupees of equities so far in September.
summary.global: The Nikkei 225 added 1.3 percent to 64,755.98 into the Bank of Japan decision due today, where swap markets price about a 98 percent chance of a quarter point move to 1.25 percent, a level last seen roughly 31 years ago, while the Hang Seng slipped 0.44 percent to 24,604.29 with gold and oil names under pressure. Europe closed higher with the DAX up 0.53 percent and the FTSE 100 up 0.28 percent after the Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75 percent on a 6 to 3 vote and voted unanimously to run the gilt portfolio down to zero over a multi year plan.

calendar.what: Bank of Japan monetary policy statement, with swaps pricing a quarter point hike to 1.25 percent. India weekly bank loan growth, deposit growth and forex reserves. Hero Motors, Jindal Supreme and SS Retail IPOs close in India.
NSE and Sonaselection India IPOs close. Bajaj Finance meets London institutional investors on 21 and 22 September.
Basis of allotment expected for the Sonaselection India IPO.
Anchor book for the A-One Steels India IPO. Bajaj Finance meets institutional investors in Boston and New York on 23 and 24 September.
A-One Steels India IPO opens at a price band of 385 to 405 rupees. NSE and Sonaselection India shares are due to list on BSE and NSE. US weekly initial jobless claims.

No scheduled macro release or watchlist earnings confirmed for this date in this run. Renaissance Capital's US IPO calendar carried no deals with confirmed dates between 18 September and 2 October at the time of this run, so the IPO table below is India only.
Outside the seven day window but on the radar: RBI Monetary Policy Committee decision, meeting 5 to 7 October 2026.
